fichas.title: Pythagorean Rectangle and Harmonic Proportions
fichas.summary: The page describes the Pythagorean rectangle as a basis for optically harmonious proportions derived from musical intervals. It includes harmonic interval proportions and excludes the disharmonic second and seventh.
uses: Relating harmonic proportions to building dimensions
Establishing geometric proportions for architectural design

There have been agreements about the dimensioning of buildings
since early times. The first specific statements date from the time
of Pythagoras, who started from the basis that the numerical
proportions found in acoustics must also be optically harmonic.
This led to the development of the Pythagorean rectangle --7 0,
which contains all the harmonic interval proportions but not the
two disharmonic intervals -the second and seventh.
Spatial measurements can be derived from these number
relationships. Pythagorean or diophantic equations produce
number groups f)- 0, which should be used for the width, height
and length of rooms:
a2 + b2 = c2
a= m (y2 -x2)
b=mx2xxxy
c=m(y2 +x2)

The geometric shapes named by Plato and Vitruvius are also of
critical importance: circle, triangle --7
and square --7 0, from
which polygonal traverses can be constructed. Each halving then
gives further polygonal traverses. Other polygonal traverses (e.g.
heptagon --7 0, nonagon --7 Cli)) can be formed only by approximation
or by superimposition. For example, a 15-sided polygon --7 0 can be
constructed by superimposing an equilateral triangle onto a pentagon.

e

The pentagon --7 0 or pentagram has a natural relationship to the
golden section, as does the derived decagon, but in earlier times
its particular dimensional relationships were hardly ever used --7
p. 32 0-0.
Polygonal traverses are necessary for the design and construction
of so-called 'round' buildings.

fichas.title: Pythagorean Triangles for Room Dimensions
fichas.summary: Pythagorean and diophantine relationships generate number groups proposed for room width, height, and length. The page gives the right-triangle equation and formulas using whole numbers x and y, with x less than y, and a magnification or reduction factor m.
uses: Deriving proportional room width, height, and length

fichas.title: Polygonal Traverses and Geometric Forms
fichas.summary: Circle, triangle, and square are presented as bases for constructing polygonal traverses. The page illustrates regular and approximated polygons, relates the pentagon and decagon to the golden section, and notes that polygonal traverses are needed to design and construct round buildings.
uses: Applying geometric forms and golden-section relationships

fichas.title: Dimensions in a Polygonal Traverse
fichas.summary: The page identifies radius r, chord c, and triangle height h as key measurements for a polygonal traverse. A diagram and accompanying formula relate these measurements using the angle β; the calculation is continued on the referenced page.
uses: Calculating dimensions in a polygonal traverse
